audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were marked Swain in both layers while whys[1] and whys[2] under them say Graves gets his kit online first and calls Level 3 'your last clean window'. Levels 4-5 and 6 were marked Skill while whys[3] and whys[4] say Swain out-values the chip and that 'the lane flips here'.
audit.why: The packet chart is Skill / Graves / Graves / Swain / Swain / Swain / Swain, which matches the written reasoning and the 41.67% Emerald+ win rate: Graves owns one short window before Demonic Ascension exists, and nothing after it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet in both layers, with phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why was Graves boilerplate about Collateral Damage, and Demonic Ascension's cooldown was never given anywhere despite being named the matchup-defining ability on six fields.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120s at every rank — it never gets shorter, unlike Graves' R which drops 100 to 80 to 60 — and Riot's text says the form 'is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions', so it is not a timed window you can simply outlast in a duel.
audit.corrected: 120s and the indefinite-while-draining condition written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5] and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page is built on a Smoke Screen blind that does not exist, and compounds it: whys[2], mid and wants.you[2] tell you to 'blind his Death's Hand autos', while mid and late both explain the blind's limits ('blinds his autos, not his abilities'). Death's Hand is an ability, not an auto-attack, so even a real blind would not touch it.
audit.why: Graves W: 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' Swain Q, Death's Hand: 'Swain unleashes several bolts of eldritch power that pierce through enemies', 750 range, 3-7s.
audit.corrected: Every blind reference replaced with the real effect — impact slow plus sight-range cut — and the value restated correctly: it stops him lining up Death's Hand because he cannot see you, not because he is blinded.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is described as a 'slow wave that roots', with no mention of the return pass.
audit.why: Riot text, Swain E: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer.' The root is on the way back, which is why players who sidestep the throw still get caught — and it is a shorter cooldown during Demonic Ascension. 850 range, 10-12s.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.you[2] and mid.

edits.before: Level 1 is even — he only has Death's Hand (Q) and you have one ability, so neither of you commits. Your real chance is the 2-3 window: once you have E and a second ability, weave in for the point-blank shell spread plus an End of the Line cone, then E straight back out, because if you sit in lane he just pokes you with Q. Never walk in a straight line at him — Nevermove (E) is a slow wave that roots, and that root is what turns Death's Hand and Vision of Empire into a free trade.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — he only has Death's Hand (Q) and you have one ability, so neither of you commits. Your real chance is the 2-3 window: once you have E and a second ability, weave in for the point-blank shell spread plus an End of the Line cone, then E straight back out, because if you sit in lane he just pokes you with Q. Never walk in a straight line at him — Nevermove (E, 850 range, 10-12s) travels out and then returns to Swain, and it is the return pass that roots, so sidestepping the throw is only half the dodge.

edits.before: This is where it slips away. By 4-5 his Q poke and passive HP from Soul Fragments wash out your chip damage, and at 6 Demonic Ascension (R) heals through your entire burst combo while recharging him for the next fight. You can still win a clean all-in if you Smoke Screen his Death's Hand autos and burst before he roots — but the instant Nevermove lands, you eat Vision of Empire and his drain grinds you down. Bait the root by feinting in with one E charge, then commit only if it whiffs. Remember Smoke Screen blinds his autos, not his abilities — Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, and the R drain all still hit.
edits.after: This is where it slips away. By 4-5 his Q poke and passive HP from Soul Fragments wash out your chip damage, and at 6 Demonic Ascension (R) heals through your entire burst combo while recharging him for the next fight. You can still win a clean all-in if you smoke him for the slow and burst before he roots — but the instant Nevermove lands, you eat Vision of Empire and his drain grinds you down. Bait the root by feinting in with one E charge and commit only if it whiffs, remembering the wave roots on the way back to him, so clearing the outgoing pass is half the job. Smoke Screen blinds nothing — it slows on impact and cuts sight range.

edits.before: Late game is his. Full-AP Swain roots you from range with Nevermove, drops Vision of Empire on top, and drains you through your True Grit stacks because his damage is percent-HP magic AOE that does not care about your armor. Your Smoke Screen blind does nothing against any of his abilities — only his basic attacks. Don't try to 1v1 him — take side waves, abuse Quickdraw mobility to skirmish elsewhere, and make sure your team never groups inside Nevermove's pull-root range.
edits.after: Late game is his. Full-AP Swain roots you from range with Nevermove, drops Vision of Empire on top, and drains you through your True Grit stacks because his damage is percent-HP magic AOE that does not care about your armor. Smoke Screen does not blind — it slows on impact and cuts sight range, so it buys a step, not a whiffed spell. Don't try to 1v1 him — take side waves, abuse Quickdraw mobility to skirmish elsewhere, and never let your team group inside Nevermove's 850 pull-root.

notes: This page had the blind error in its most damaging form: it told the reader to blind Death's Hand — which is an ability, not an auto-attack — and then twice explained the blind's supposed limits, so a reader would come away confident about a mechanic that does not exist in either direction. Best real addition: Nevermove roots on the RETURN pass, not the outgoing one, which is the single most common way players get caught in this matchup. Level chart sides in both layers argued against their own whys and are now aligned to the packet chart and the 41.67% win rate.
